title: procurement-ready-sku-storyboard-dedicated-inference
content:
Executive summary:
A compact, procurement-ready narrative that articulates the value of Redwood Dedicated for enterprise cloud and regulated customers. Focus: SLA-backed latency/availability guarantees, tenant isolation and data control, and predictable throughput pricing that aligns to procurement needs (commit + headroom). This doc is a storyboard for sales + deals teams to use in discovery and legal negotiations — includes objection responses, contract phrasing snippets, and a procurement checklist.

Audience:
- Procurement and vendor evaluation teams (buyers)
- Platform/infra architects reviewing isolation and SLAs
- Legal/infosec teams validating data controls
- Sales execs and AE/SE deal leads prepping procurement conversations

Key framing (single line):
"Reserved inference capacity with SLA-backed performance and enterprise isolation — predictable economics for production LLM workloads."

Top-level value props (elevator bullets):
- Predictable throughput: committed GPU pool with measured per-second token throughput guarantees (p95/p99 targets by model class).
- Commercial SLAs: uptime and latency SLOs tied to credits, with defined remediation and escalations for sustained miss.
- Tenant & data isolation: dedicated VPCs, optional on-prem package, and KMS/HSM integration for key separation.
- Operational controls: burst policies, capacity failover routing, and rollback/automatic fallback to compatible model variants.
- Cost control: commit-based discounts, flexible burst billing, and tooling to optimize batching and quantization for unit cost reduction.

Procurement playbook (short):
1) Discovery goals: quantify peak qps, batch vs. streaming usage, model families, latency targets (p95 latency budget), data residency and encryption needs.
2) Offer structure: base monthly commitment (reserved GPUs/slots) + burst pool (consumption overage at discounted burst price) + optional SRE on-call support add-on.
3) SLA tiers: Standard (99.5% uptime, latency p95 SLO), Premium (99.9% uptime, tighter latency SLO, 24/7 response), Enterprise (custom SLOs, dedicated support).
4) Negotiation levers: term length (1y/3y), commit size, early termination fees, support hours, dedicated on-prem appliance option.

SLA & metrics (narrative + measurable items):
- Availability: measured at the regional service endpoint level, rolling 30d window. Example: Standard SLA = 99.5% region availability; credit formula: pro-rata service credits based on outage minutes beyond threshold.
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 generation latency measured on representative model family; latency SLA applies to pinned model family/sequence-length profile specified in SoW.
- Throughput: guaranteed sustained throughput expressed in tokens-per-second or concurrent request units for a pinned model class; documented warmup profile and cache priming expectations.
- Incident response: defined on-call windows, RTO for critical incidents, and escalation path to account-level SRE.

Sample contract phrasing (snippets for legal):
- "Service Availability" clause: "Supplier shall maintain Service Availability of at least 99.5% during each monthly measurement period for the Dedicated Capacity provided under this Agreement. Service Availability is measured at the regional public endpoint and excludes scheduled maintenance with prior notice."

- "Latency SLO" clause: "Supplier will use commercially reasonable efforts to ensure that p95 inference latency for the agreed model family and input profile does not exceed [X]ms. In the event of sustained misses (greater than N minutes in a rolling 7-day window), customer may claim service credits as defined in Section Y."

- "Data Isolation" clause: "Dedicated Capacity will be deployed in a single-tenant GPU pool within the Customer-specified VPC or the Supplier-managed equivalent. Customer data processed by Dedicated Capacity will not be used to train or improve Supplier models, and keys are managed via Customer KMS where requested."

Common procurement objections + suggested responses (short Q/A):
- "We need 100% uptime." -> Response: 100% uptime for globally-distributed services is impractical; offer multi-region redundancy + financial credit and runbooks. For highly regulated customers we can provide private on-prem option with custom redundancy built into the SoW.
- "What if you change the model and performance drops?" -> Response: Customers pin model versions for Dedicated; rollouts are controlled by the customer and model changes are opt-in. Auto-fallback to previously-pinned variant is included in rollout policy.
- "How do you prove throughput?" -> Response: Include benchmark annex in contract, run joint acceptance testing (CAT) with customer workloads, and provide per-token cost/latency dashboards for the entire contract term.
- "Can we audit?" -> Response: Yes — provide SOC2 reports, KMS/HSM integration proof, and offer specific audit windows for enterprise customers (subject to NDA and scheduling).

Competitive notes (short analysis vs representative vendors):
- Cloud-managed endpoints (major clouds): strength = ecosystem integration and global scale; weakness = higher per-token op-ex costs, less opinionated latency guarantees for LLMs. Lean into Redwood's inference-optimized runtime and model-aware batching as cost/latency differentiator.
- LLM API providers: strength = simplicity; weakness = limited enterprise isolation and fewer procurement-grade SLAs. Position Redwood as bridging API simplicity with enterprise-grade guarantees.
- Self-hosted runtimes: strength = control; weakness = ops burden and slower provisioning. Emphasize Redwood Dedicated removes ops burden while retaining control over capacity and isolation.

Quantitative framing examples (talking points for AE):
- "Customer X replaced ad-hoc cloud endpoints with a 12-month reserved pool and achieved 38% lower token cost and 2x predictable 99th percentile tail latency improvements for peak inference." (anecdotal placeholder to be replaced with reference customers in final deck).
- "Commit + burst model typically reduces effective per-token cost by 25–45% vs pay-as-you-go at scale — exact mix depends on burst profile and batchability."

Deal-level checklist (procurement handoff):
- Confirm pinned models and expected input profile (avg token length, image vs text, streaming needs)
- Establish measurement plan: SLO measurement endpoints, reporting cadence, and acceptance test annex
- Define commit sizing and burst rules, overage pricing, and true-up cadence
- Security attachments: encryption-in-transit, encryption-at-rest, KMS integration, SOC2/Security docs
- Support & escalation: on-call hours, SLAs for RTO/RPO, named account SRE if in contract
- IP & data usage: explicit non-use clause for customer data, data deletion timelines post-termination

Tactics for AE/SE during procurement meetings (short):
- Bring a short technical appendix showing how warm caches and batching affect throughput numbers; demonstrate a reproducible load test plan.
- Offer joint pilot/acceptance tests with real customer prompts; convert acceptance thresholds into contract annex.
- If procurement pushes for lower price, trade on commitment length and early-payment terms vs support coverage and credit terms.

Sample procurement email (one-paragraph template):
"Hi <Procurement Name>, following our chat, attached is a short proposal for Dedicated Inference capacity that includes SSE-grade isolation and SLA options. Key items: a 12-month reserved pool matched to your peak qps, a 20% burst buffer, and a Premium SLA option with 24/7 support. We recommend running a two-week acceptance test to validate throughput and latency on your real workloads — happy to schedule with our SRE team. — Priya"

Open items / TODOs:
- Replace placeholder customer numbers with anonymized reference cases and validated delta metrics.
- Draft a standard acceptance test annex and load test script to include as linked artifact.
- Legal: finalize credit calculation language and maintenance window definitions.

Notes to self / friction points observed in pilot deals:
- Procurement frequently conflates availability SLAs with latency SLAs; separate the metrics early and show a clear measurement endpoint.
- Security teams often want proof-of-isolation; provide short runbook + architecture diagram in deck.
- CFOs focus on effective unit economics; include a simple 2-line ROI calculation in the commercial proposal.

Next steps (immediate):
- Iterate this doc with AE team feeds from three active deals (due by 2026-03-07).
- Prep a one-page acceptance test annex and benchmark script (Engineering owner: Marco).
- Update Confluence and attach final contract snippets after legal review.

End of storyboard.
